uncited: NeRF Editing and Inpainting Procedures modify a pre-trained Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) to remove objects, fill occluded regions, or alter appearance and geometry based on user intent [17712-inpainting-and-object-removal.md][12491-nerf-editing-procedure.md].

Unlike standard training which reconstructs a scene from scratch, these methods optimize existing parameters to satisfy new constraints while maintaining multi-view consistency [17712-inpainting-and-object-removal.md].

They are distinguished from sibling methods by their reliance on external 2D priors (such as inpainted images or diffusion models) to guide 3D optimization, rather than relying solely on multi-view geometry or semantic segmentation alone [17712-inpainting-and-object-removal.md].

All methods in this family operate on a pre-trained NeRF representation $f_\theta: (\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \to (\sigma, \mathbf{c})$, where $\mathbf{x}$ is a 3D coordinate, $\mathbf{d}$ is the viewing direction, $\sigma$ is volume density, and $\mathbf{c}$ is color [Parent].

The core mechanism involves an optimization loop that minimizes a loss function $L$ to update the NeRF parameters $\theta$ (or a subset thereof) [17712-inpainting-and-object-removal.md][14393-semantic-and-language-guided-editing.md].

**Masking/Selection:** A binary or probabilistic mask $M$ or selection field identifies the region of interest (ROI) or occluded areas, typically user-defined via sketching or language instructions [14393-semantic-and-language-guided-editing.md].

**External Priors:** Methods rely on 2D priors to guide 3D changes, commonly using diffusion guidance (e.g., Score Distillation Sampling from text-to-image models) or semantic/text features (e.g., CLIP or LSeg) to align rendered features with prompts [14393-semantic-and-language-guided-editing.md][17712-inpainting-and-object-removal.md].

**View Consistency Enforcement:** To prevent inconsistencies across views, methods enforce multi-view constraints through implicit geometrical and photometric priors embodied by the neural network, which automatically propagates single-view edits to all views [14393-semantic-and-language-guided-editing.md].

Key developments include the introduction of diffusion-guided editing (e.g., RePaint-NeRF, Instruct-NeRF2NeRF) which leveraged 2D generative models to guide 3D optimization [14365-repaint-nerf.md][15089-instruct-nerf2nerf-optimization.md].
Subsequent methods like Blended-NeRF and NeRF-Art introduced techniques for localized editing and stylization using text prompts and volumetric blending [12273-blended-nerf.md][13438-nerf-art.md].

Recent advancements focus on improving multi-view consistency through semantic priors and progressive inpainting strategies [8658-progressive-inpainting-and-erasing.md][14393-semantic-and-language-guided-editing.md].
